title: A Divided Crowd at the Festival
overview: At a major festival in Jerusalem, Jesus teaches openly while crowds argue over who he is and the religious leaders try and fail to arrest him.

parts.label: Doubting brothers (vv. 1-9)
parts.note: The Festival of Tabernacles was an autumn harvest feast when people lived in simple shelters to remember Israel's years in the wilderness, and Jerusalem filled with pilgrims. Jesus' brothers, who did not yet believe in him, push him to make a public show there, but he says his "time" has not come, which many readers take to mean he would act on God's timing rather than theirs.

parts.label: Whispers in the crowd (vv. 10-13)
parts.note: Jesus goes up quietly, without drawing attention, while people murmur about whether he is a good man or a fraud. No one speaks up for him openly because they fear the leaders who oppose him.

parts.label: Teaching in the temple (vv. 14-24)
parts.note: People are amazed that he teaches so well without having trained under a recognised teacher, and he says his teaching comes from God, who sent him. He points out that boys were circumcised even on the Sabbath, the weekly day of rest, so condemning him for healing a whole person on that day makes no sense, recalling the man he healed in chapter 5.

parts.label: Where is he from? (vv. 25-36)
parts.note: Some believed the Messiah, the king God promised, would appear from nowhere, so knowing Jesus came from an ordinary family in Galilee seemed to rule him out. When he says he is going where they cannot follow, they guess he means Jewish communities scattered in Greek cities, while Christians read it as pointing to his death and return to God.

parts.label: Living water (vv. 37-44)
parts.note: During this festival priests carried water from the Pool of Siloam and poured it at the altar with great celebration, and many readers connect Jesus' cry about drinking from him with that ritual, though John does not say so. John explains that the "rivers of living water" meant God's Spirit, which believers would receive later, and scholars are unsure exactly which scripture Jesus is quoting.

parts.label: Guards return empty-handed (vv. 45-53)
parts.note: The guards sent to arrest him come back saying no one ever spoke like this, and the leaders scorn both them and the crowd, while Nicodemus insists the law requires a fair hearing first. Verse 53 begins a story (8:1-11) that the earliest manuscripts do not include.

disagreement: Because the Greek of verse 38 can be punctuated two ways, Christians differ on whether the rivers of living water flow from within the believer or from Jesus himself.
think: The crowd split over Jesus, and many kept their view to themselves out of fear of those in charge; what makes it hard to give someone a fair hearing when the people around you have already made up their minds?
